message.reasoning:
I need to decide whether to accept, reject, or counter a trade offer in Monopoly.

Reviewing the current holdings and trade history to evaluate the offer.

The trade history and current holdings appear inconsistent. p1 still shows Water Works but Virginia is missing. p3 owns Virginia yet Water Works is absent. I need to resolve this discrepancy before evaluating the offer.

The trade history is confusingly worded. The current game state is authoritative.

Mapping the remaining monopolies. p3 holds St Charles and Virginia, blocking my States Avenue. p1 holds St James and Tennessee, blocking my New York. p2 holds Ventnor, Pacific, and North Carolina, but lacks Pennsylvania Avenue. Boardwalk is dark blue.

p3 also owns Illinois, leaving Indiana and Kentucky split between us. p2 holds Ventnor, so the yellow group is split between me and p2 with Atlantic unowned.

The offer is to give up New York Avenue for $400, Short Line, and Electric Company.

p1 would gain the orange monopoly with three houses on each property. Rent would reach $750 to $1,000 per house and $950 per hotel. Building nine houses costs $900. p1 would have $492 cash after the trade and could mortgage Short Line or Electric Company to cover the cost.

Mortgaging Vermont, Connecticut, and Water Works would raise enough cash to build three houses on New York. This confirms the trade is extremely dangerous.

I have rejected every prior offer for New York because of this exact risk. The return is only $400 cash plus one of four railroads and a utility with weak rent. I will reject this offer.

I cannot counter this offer because any counter that includes New York would be rejected. I will reject it outright. I am not desperate to escape jail with $408 cash and no get-out-of-jail-free card.

I will reject the offer with a firm public message. I considered asking for St James or Tennessee instead of New York to break p1's orange pair, but that would still weaken my position.
